quarterly_data.signal: Eli Lilly's 10-K: 2025 revenue was $65,179 million, up 45% from $45,043 million in 2024 (U.S. $43,481 million, up 43%; outside U.S. $21,698 million, up 48%), net income was $20,640 million (up 95%) and diluted EPS $22.95 (up 96%). By product, Mounjaro revenue was $22,965 million (up 99%), Zepbound $13,542 million (up 175%) and Verzenio $5,723 million (up 8%). Gross margin was 83.0% of revenue versus 81.3%. By region, Europe revenue was $11,558 million, Japan $2,132 million and China $1,951 million. Jardiance, which in its most significant markets remains in the Boehringer Ingelheim collaboration through December 31, 2028, contributed $3,432 million of collaboration revenue.
quarterly_data.figure: 2025 revenue $65,179 million (+45%); net income $20,640 million; EPS $22.95; Mounjaro $22,965 million (+99%); Zepbound $13,542 million (+175%); Verzenio $5,723 million; gross margin 83.0%; Jardiance $3,432 million

quarterly_data.signal: Eli Lilly's 10-K: under the Inflation Reduction Act, HHS selected Jardiance (part of the Boehringer Ingelheim collaboration) in August 2023 as one of the first ten medicines subject to government-set prices effective in 2026, and in January 2026 selected Trulicity and Verzenio as additional medicines subject to government-set prices to be effective in 2028. Lilly says that, given its product portfolio, it expects other significant products will be selected in future years.
quarterly_data.figure: Jardiance government-set price effective 2026; Trulicity and Verzenio effective 2028
